name: Ish-bosheth (Saul's son)
title: Saul's successor over Israel
summary: Ish-bosheth was the son of King Saul and was installed as king over Israel by the commander Abner after Saul's death. His short reign was marked by civil war against David, who ruled over Judah. He was eventually murdered by two of his own officers, paving the way for David's rule over all Israel.

keyEvents.title: Appointed King by Abner
keyEvents.description: After Saul's death, the commander Abner took Ish-bosheth and brought him to Mahanaim, where he was appointed king over Israel. He was forty years old at that time and reigned for two years.

keyEvents.title: Civil War with David
keyEvents.description: Ish-bosheth's reign as king was marked by a long war between the house of Saul and the house of David. David's side grew steadily stronger while the house of Saul became weaker.

keyEvents.title: Conflict with Abner over Rizpah
keyEvents.description: Ish-bosheth confronted Abner for having slept with Saul's concubine Rizpah. This led the offended Abner to decide to switch allegiance to David.

keyEvents.title: Lost Courage after Abner's Death
keyEvents.description: When Ish-bosheth heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he lost courage, and all Israel was dismayed. Without his powerful commander, his position was weakened.

keyEvents.title: Murdered by Rechab and Baana
keyEvents.description: Two of Ish-bosheth's commanders, Rechab and Baana, entered his house at midday while he was resting and stabbed him in the belly. They took his head to David in Hebron.

keyEvents.title: David Punishes the Murderers
keyEvents.description: David had Rechab and Baana executed for killing a righteous man in his own house. Ish-bosheth's head was buried in Abner's tomb in Hebron.
